title: Presenting a protection-order claim to a rental platform or social housing office once, not per listing
moment: A survivor searching for a new rental applies to many listings through a rental platform and a city social-housing or rent-subsidy office, each of which wants the order shown to qualify her for priority placement, deposit waiver or subsidy. Every landlord she applies to receives a fresh copy, and the same document lets them recognise her across unrelated applications.
verifier: City housing bureau or rent-subsidy office, and rental platforms offering a priority or reduced-deposit channel
predicate: Holder is currently covered by an active protection order for the next lease-start window, shown as a presentation bound to the specific verifier and application.
disclosed_today: A copy of the order or a social worker letter with her name, ID number, and case details, given repeatedly to multiple parties who can compare and match the copies.
issuer: The municipal 家庭暴力暨性侵害防治中心 or a contracted women's shelter (such as a 婦女救援基金會 branch) signing the attestation.
why_zk: The credential should work only for the party and context it was presented to, like a SameSite-restricted cookie, so that two landlords or a landlord and a platform cannot match her across applications. Zero-knowledge presentations that are unlinkable and verifier-bound give this directly, where a copied PDF cannot. Weakness: the housing office may legitimately need to confirm identity for subsidy payment, so that disclosure still occurs there; the unlinkability benefit is mostly against private landlords and platforms.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In SameSite cookies, an attribute limits a stored credential to requests from the issuing context so third parties cannot recognise the browser across sites; here, a verifier-bound, unlinkable presentation plays that attribute so each landlord or platform sees the claim only in its own application.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A stored credential should be presented only to the party that issued it in the current context, but the browser sends it on any request the context triggers, so an unrelated observer can match the holder across contexts. | mechanism: The SameSite cookie attribute, which limits the cookie to same-site requests (Strict, Lax, or None); the IETF draft describes it as a per-cookie setting, and cross-site behaviour depends on the chosen value.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the foreign-investor account opening, an agent hands over a full ID copy to prove they are a real identified person with no alternative stated; here, the survivor's copied order or social-worker letter plays that role, replaced by a signed claim that proves standing without the full document.

title: Strike authorization vote at a TSMC-supplier factory union
moment: A Taoyuan electronics-plant enterprise union holds a strike authorization ballot over a bargaining impasse. Members queue at the canteen with their employee badge; today the union checks them against the dues roster, which includes names, employee IDs and department, and management-side HR is often asked to confirm staff status, so the employer can infer who showed up or abstained.
verifier: The enterprise union's election committee running the strike ballot
predicate: Holder is a current dues-paying member of this union (dues paid through the last billing month) and has not yet cast a ballot in this vote round (one-time nullifier).
disclosed_today: Full name, employee ID, department and shift, national ID number against the dues roster, plus a signature on a paper sign-in sheet that HR or foremen can sometimes see.
issuer: The union itself (its membership office), co-signing dues status from its payroll-deduction ledger
why_zk: The union must verify membership and one-person-one-vote, but the employer must never learn who voted. A membership proof with a per-ballot nullifier gives eligibility and once-only without a name linking to the ballot. Weakness: the union already knows its own members, so the gain is mainly against employer observation and roster leaks, and in-person queues remain observable regardless of the cryptography.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In Taiwan's Digital Identity Wallet, the user picks which fields to release per scenario after scanning a QR code; here, the union member's wallet releases only a membership-and-not-yet-voted proof at the ballot station instead of the whole badge record.

title: Deposit-free rental application through a rental platform or NGO housing service
moment: A worker who just changed employer through a transfer in Kaohsiung applies via an NGO-run housing matching service to rent a shared flat with a reduced deposit. The agent asks for the new employer's permit transfer approval, ARC, and pay history to prove stability, and forwards the bundle to several landlords at once.
verifier: NGO or commercial rental matching platform forwarding applications to landlords
predicate: Holder's work authorisation with a sponsoring employer was valid at a time no more than 3 days ago, bound to a one-time application nonce so it cannot be forwarded and reused with other landlords (freshness plus unlinkability).
disclosed_today: Whole application bundle: ARC, transfer approval letter, employer details, payslips, forwarded to every landlord contacted.
issuer: Ministry of Labor Workforce Development Agency, or an authorised employer-side HR platform issuing signed status for each application.
why_zk: Each landlord needs one bit of fresh status; the bundle forwarded to many parties lets them match the worker across listings and keep stale copies after the worker moves. Per-application nonces keep each presentation to its own verifier. Weakness: a worker mid-transfer has a gap in status that the registry may not reflect quickly, so freshness could wrongly fail exactly the people who most need housing.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In SameSite cookies, a credential is sent on any triggered request so third parties can recognise the browser across contexts; here, the forwarded application bundle plays the cookie and the per-landlord nonce plays the SameSite restriction.

title: Cremation arrangement without photocopying the whole family register
moment: After a death in a Taipei household, the eldest son goes to a funeral home to sign the cremation and service contract. Staff photocopy his national ID and the deceased's household registration transcript (戶籍謄本), which lists parents, spouse, siblings and children, to confirm he is the right next of kin to authorise cremation.
verifier: Funeral home (殯葬業者) handling cremation authorisation
predicate: Holder is a next of kin of the named deceased, and no living kin of higher priority (spouse, then adult children, then parents, and so on) exists who has not consented or been accounted for.
disclosed_today: Full ID copy of the signer, plus a household registration transcript showing every household member's name, ID number, birth date, address, marital status and family ties.
issuer: Household Registration Office (戶政事務所, Ministry of the Interior), signing a kin-rank attestation derived from the register.
why_zk: The funeral home needs only the signer's rank in the order of kin, not the whole family tree. A signed attestation of relationship and priority rank, shown through selective disclosure, replaces the full transcript. It is weaker where the order depends on facts not in the register (estrangement, unregistered partners, disputes among siblings of equal rank), so the proof can establish priority from the register but cannot settle a family dispute.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the EUDI Wallet recital, the holder discloses only some attributes of an attestation to a relying party; here, the household-registry kin-rank attestation plays that role, revealing only 'next of kin, rank 1' and not the rest of the family record.
claimed_borrowings.source_excerpt: A verifier needs one attribute from a larger identity record, but the holder cannot share just that attribute from the record. | mechanism: Selective disclosure of attributes from electronic attestations held in the EU Digital Identity Wallet.

title: Peer-vouched volunteer for a one-day temple festival children's activity
moment: Ahead of a temple festival in Kaohsiung, a church-linked youth group lends a dozen parents and teens to run a children's craft corner for a single day. There is no time to order official certificates for everyone. The temple volunteer lead asks for ID copies and a handwritten declaration and writes down names and phone numbers.
verifier: The temple volunteer lead running the festival children's corner
predicate: The helper has no child-related conviction, attested by a trusted community or school body that has itself checked the record (non-membership, peer or community issuer)
disclosed_today: ID card copy, phone number and a handwritten self-declaration on paper, which the lead cannot verify, kept in a personal notebook
issuer: A community body such as the youth group's parent organisation or a school that already holds a recent criminal-record check for its own volunteers and countersigns a short-lived credential
why_zk: This is weak to moderate. A proof is only worth the trust placed in the signing body, and a youth group's attestation is not an official check, so the temple gains less assurance than with a state-issued credential. The benefit is that it replaces unverifiable paper declarations and ID copies with a signed yes/no that the helper presents unlinkably; if the group's own checking is sloppy, the zero-knowledge layer adds privacy but not truth.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In attorney-client privilege, an essential third party such as an interpreter may be present without destroying confidentiality; here, the youth group as vouching issuer plays that essential-intermediary role, and the temple lead sees only the outcome, not the record behind it.

title: Company dormitory operator checking a worker still belongs to a sponsoring employer at monthly re-lease
moment: A third-party dormitory operator in Taichung leases beds to several small factories' migrant workers. Each month, before renewing bed allocation and a subsidised meal bundle, the front desk photocopies the worker's ARC and asks the broker for an updated employer letter, since workers who change employer or leave the permit can no longer legally be housed under the factory-block contract.
verifier: Dormitory operator / dorm manager serving multiple employers' workers
predicate: Freshness: on the date of renewal, the holder is legally employed by a sponsoring employer (permit active and not in transfer, termination or absconder status), proven by an attestation signed within the last 7 days
disclosed_today: Photocopied ARC (ID number, birthdate, address), employer letter with company tax ID and contract dates, sometimes broker's file listing wages and deductions, stored in a paper binder at the front desk
issuer: Workforce Development Agency permit registry, or the sponsoring employer's e-signature via a government-recognised issuer, expiring after 7 days
why_zk: A short expiry makes the claim a real freshness check: a worker who was dismissed last week cannot present an old photocopy as proof. The operator learns yes/no plus the employer's pseudonymous ID for billing, not the ARC, address or wages. Honest limit: the operator is legally required in some circumstances to keep a copy of the ARC for fire-safety and police registers, so full minimisation only works if regulators accept the attestation in place of the copy, and a coerced worker has no real power to refuse the paper route.

title: Juror or lay-judge candidate proves summons for today's session at the Taiwan High Court's new lay-participation trial desk
moment: A citizen called as a prospective lay judge (國民法官) for a trial at a district court arrives for the selection day. The security desk today photocopies or records the summons and national ID to ensure only the called pool enters the secured area, while the candidate's identity is supposed to be shielded from the public and parties.
verifier: Court security desk handling the lay-judge candidate pool entrance, plus the clerk seating them
predicate: Holder is one of the candidates called for this specific selection session (membership in the called pool), without revealing name or ID number to the entrance desk.
disclosed_today: Name, national ID number, address on the summons, and sometimes a scanned copy of the summons and ID kept in the desk's attendance record.
issuer: The district court administering the lay-judge candidate list (the court's lay-judge office), signing pool membership
why_zk: Identities of lay-judge candidates are legally sensitive and the entrance desk only needs pool membership. A membership proof lets the desk admit people without keeping a list of names and ID numbers, reducing risk of leaks or pressure on candidates. Weakness: the courtroom clerk later must know who each person is to run selection and record attendance, so identity is revealed eventually; the benefit is limited to the first perimeter checkpoint and retention of copies, and the law on required ID checks for attendance may still demand a visual check.

title: Cremation booking: next-of-kin rank without a family-tree dump
moment: A daughter walks into a funeral home in Taichung the morning after her father dies at home, to sign the cremation authorization. The director must confirm she is the highest-ranking living next of kin (e.g. spouse is deceased, she is an adult child), and today photocopies the deceased's household registration transcript showing every relative, ID numbers, addresses and marital history.
verifier: Private funeral home (殯葬業者) arranging cremation
predicate: Holder is a member of the set of persons who are the deceased's highest-priority living next of kin under the applicable priority order (spouse, then children, then parents, etc.), with no higher-ranking relative alive.
disclosed_today: Full household registration transcript (戶籍謄本) of the deceased, with ID numbers, birthdates, addresses, parents, spouse and all siblings, plus a copy of the applicant's national ID card front and back.
issuer: Ministry of the Interior household registration office (戶政事務所), signing a kin-rank credential derived from the registry when the death is registered.
why_zk: Rank is a membership claim over a registry the household office already holds, so a signed credential could state only 'holder is first-priority next of kin of deceased X' with the wallet proving it. This mirrors the Swiss e-ID idea of sharing only the needed attribute rather than the whole record. Weakness: it needs the household office to issue such credentials at death registration, and the funeral home may still be legally expected to retain a document copy, so adoption depends on regulator acceptance.

claimed_borrowings.borrowed_aspect: In the Swiss e-ID, selective disclosure releases only the one attribute a transaction needs from a whole credential; here, the household registration record plays the whole credential and 'first-priority next of kin' is the single attribute released.
